title: Drain VCF Automation requests before rotating a looked-up vSphere credential
prompt:
Implement `src/VcfAutomationCredentialRotator.java` as a dependency-free, single-file Java 17 client that rotates the password of a named VCF Automation 9.1 vSphere cloud account without stranding requests already in progress on the old password. Preserve the public constructor, method, exception and record declarations in the starter file. Use only the Java 17 standard library; do not add another production source file.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation. It has no published specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, so the focused contract was derived from the authoritative Broadcom xAPIs reference pages recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. The contract states plainly that it comes from reference documentation rather than a published specification. Its four local operation slugs are not vendor-published operationIds. Contact only those four operations.

Construction performs no traffic. Validate the origin, bearer token, API version and poll interval as declared by the starter API. `rotate(accountName, newPassword)` validates both arguments before traffic and performs this workflow in order:

1. Call `listRequestTrackers` exactly once. Remember, in response order, every tracker whose status is `INPROGRESS`. Poll each remembered tracker by its returned `id` until it first becomes `FINISHED` or `FAILED`. A failed drain aborts before any account lookup or update. Do not poll trackers that were already terminal. No cloud-account update may be sent until all remembered in-flight trackers are terminal.
2. Call `listVSphereCloudAccounts` exactly once and select exactly one account by ordinal, case-sensitive `name`. The account identifier is runtime data: every later use of an account id must use the id returned by this lookup. Preserve the selected account's required `name`, `hostName`, and enabled regions. Preserve `description`, `dcid`, and `username` only when each is present. Convert every read-side enabled region to the documented write shape containing only `name` and `externalRegionId`.
3. Call `updateVSphereCloudAccountAsync` once at the selected account's returned id. Add only `password` with `newPassword`; the old password is neither returned by the lookup nor accepted as an input. Omit every other update field. Optional values that were absent stay absent rather than becoming `null`, an empty string, list or object. Require HTTP 202 and take the update request id from that response.
4. Poll `getRequestTracker` using exactly that returned update request id until its first terminal status. Return the declared immutable `RotationResult` on `FINISHED`; throw `RotationFailedException` with the tracker id on `FAILED`.

Every call includes exactly one `apiVersion` query parameter with the configured value, one `Accept: application/json`, and one `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. GETs are bodyless and have no `Content-Type`. The PATCH has compact UTF-8 JSON, `Content-Type: application/json`, and a fixed content length. Encode every identifier as one RFC 3986 UTF-8 path segment. Do not send `$top`, `$skip`, an empty query value, a bare `?`, the old password, or the new password anywhere except the PATCH body. Require the success status documented for each operation and reject malformed success bodies, missing required values, duplicate account names, duplicate identifiers in a lookup, and unknown tracker statuses. Preserve the interrupt flag when propagating interruption. Error text must not disclose the bearer token, new password, response body, or nested transport message.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier compiles only this production file with `javac --release 17` and drives it through `tests/TestMain.java`. `TestMain` starts the supplied contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port. The mock derives its complete route allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, serves no unnamed operation, generates account and tracker identifiers at runtime, and exposes a synchronized request log. Verification checks the ordered drain, exact wire shape, read-to-write region projection, absent optional fields, secret placement, terminal failure handling, immutable output, and identifier provenance. The provenance verifier fails if a PATCH account id was not returned by that client's account lookup, or if a polled tracker id was not returned by its request-tracker lookup or PATCH response; the suite also exercises that verifier with a deliberately mismatched transcript to prove it fails closed. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/`, `tests/`, and `docs/` is protected. Edit only `src/VcfAutomationCredentialRotator.java`.

verification.network: loopback only; the verifier binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and contacts no live VMware endpoint
requirements: JDK 17 or newer (javac and java on PATH)
